findings.title: Buyer can be charged twice for one offer: a second checkout is allowed while a capture is pending, and two approved orders captured concurrently are both charged
findings.description:
There are two ways to charge a buyer twice for the same offer.

1. A buyer whose payment is under review can pay again. `start_checkout` blocks a new checkout only through `_user_owns_offer`, which counts only `active`/`completed` enrollments. While the first order is `pending` (PayPal PENDING_REVIEW, which also happens to new merchants and guest card payments), the buyer can start and pay a second order. When the first capture later completes, the `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED` webhook (`_handle_event`, lines 641-661) and reconciliation (`refresh_order` -> `_record` -> `fulfill_order`) fulfill it directly. Neither path runs `_owned_through_other_order`, and that check could not stop it anyway, because the money is already captured.

2. Two approved orders captured at the same time are both charged (two tabs, or the return page and the CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED webhook). `_owned_through_other_order` (lines 403-415, called at line 443) runs under a per-order lock only. Both captures pass the check before either is fulfilled, and both call PayPal capture.

In both cases the frontend reports success twice and the admin sees two `paid` charges.
findings.evidence:
Live, PayPal mock, offer 2 (12.50 USD):

(a) User audit_erin (id 11):
- Capture 1 (approved with outcome=PENDING) -> {"status":"pending"}.
- Second checkout while the first is pending -> 200 {"order_uuid":"0263f7a5-..."}; capture 2 -> {"status":"paid"}.
- `POST /mock/captures/TZZJCNNY4HZ1NXIYY/complete` -> webhook.
- Result: order 1 paid 12.5, order 2 paid 12.5. PayPal: [('TZZJCNNY4HZ1NXIYY','COMPLETED','12.50')] and [('WP2SFBJ37X2JEZOGP','COMPLETED','12.50')].

(b) User audit_carol (id 9): two checkouts, both approved, captures fired in two threads:
- capture B 200 {"status":"paid"}; capture A 200 {"status":"paid"}
- mock order A COMPLETED [('YH8A9AICNKV0V4C1W','COMPLETED','12.50')]
- mock order B COMPLETED [('AQVZ0EN1W1GP74SGO','COMPLETED','12.50')]
findings.suggested_fix:
1. In `start_checkout`, answer 409 {code:'PAYMENT_PENDING'} when the user has an order for the same offer in status `pending`, or `approved` within the last few minutes.
2. Serialize capture per (user_id, offer_id), not per order: take the Redis lock on `sc_pay:capture_lock:{user}:{offer}`, or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` the enrollment row before `_owned_through_other_order`, and hold it across the provider capture.
3. When `fulfill_order` finds that another order already granted the same enrollment, mark the new order as a duplicate (e.g. `raw.duplicate_of` plus an admin-visible flag) so it can be refunded, instead of silently treating it as a normal sale.

findings.title: Refunding the duplicate charge revokes the buyer's access although another order for the same offer is still paid
findings.description:
All orders of a (user, offer) pair reuse one enrollment row (`start_checkout` picks the latest one). `fulfill_order` (lines 354-367) overwrites `enrollment.provider_specific_data.order_uuid` with whichever order was fulfilled last. `revoke_order` revokes the enrollment when `data.order_uuid == order.order_uuid`, without checking whether another order for the same enrollment is still paid.

After a double charge (previous finding), the admin refunds the extra payment. If that is the order fulfilled last, the buyer loses access while still having one paid, unrefunded order. Reaching the fulfilled order otherwise would need a manual DB fix, so the buyer is locked out of content they paid for. The usergroup cleanup has the same effect, because it is keyed on enrollments in ACCESS_STATUSES.
findings.evidence:
Live, user audit_dave (id 10):
- Two concurrent captures. Completion order [('B','bb9a20b9-...','paid'), ('A','30741270-...','paid')], so A was fulfilled last.
- Refunded A's capture CMP6DULSL55OZV1XO via the mock.
- Result: `order A 30741270-... refunded`, `order B bb9a20b9-... paid`, and GET /payments/1/access -> {"for_sale":true,"has_access":false,"reason":"none","offers_count":1}.

Code (fulfillment.py:464): `if data.get("order_uuid") in (None, order.order_uuid) and enrollment.status in ACCESS_STATUSES: enrollment.status = "refunded"`
findings.suggested_fix: In `revoke_order`, before revoking the enrollment, check for another order with the same `enrollment_id` in PAID_STATUSES. If one exists, keep the enrollment active and point `provider_specific_data.order_uuid` at that order. Apply the same rule to the usergroup removal. Better still, do not let a second fulfillment overwrite `order_uuid` (see the duplicate marking suggested above).

findings.title: Sandbox PayPal configuration is accepted in production: anyone with a free sandbox account gets real, permanent access
findings.description:
`ENVIRONMENTS = ("sandbox", "live")` is allowed whatever `development_mode` says. A sandbox config is fully active for real buyers: `checkout_providers`, `start_checkout` and capture all use it.

The deploy guide (docs/despliegue.md section 7.3, step 1) tells Hilda to test on the production platform with "Entorno: Pruebas (sandbox)" against real offers. During that window, or permanently if switching to live is forgotten, anyone can create a PayPal sandbox personal account at developer.paypal.com, pay with fake money and get the course. The public `GET /payments/1/checkout/providers` tells everyone the store is in sandbox mode.

Orders and enrollments do not record the environment, so after switching to live these enrollments stay `active` forever. Nothing marks or revokes them, and they appear in overview and transactions as real sales.
findings.evidence:
Anonymous GET /api/v1/payments/1/checkout/providers -> 200 [{"provider":"paypal","label":"PayPal","environment":"sandbox","client_id":"mock-client",...}].

configs.py:95-101 accepts environment 'sandbox' with no development-mode check. paypal.py:100 `self.environment = environment if environment in ("sandbox", "live") else "sandbox"` (it even defaults to sandbox).

The PaymentsOrder model has no environment column.

despliegue.md 7.3: "Primero en sandbox: ... configura la tarjeta con Entorno: Pruebas (sandbox). Compra una oferta..."
findings.suggested_fix:
When `development_mode` is false:
- either refuse `environment='sandbox'`;
- or, in sandbox, allow checkout only to org admins/maintainers (403 for everyone else), and return a test-mode flag so the frontend shows a banner.

Also store the environment on each order and enrollment (e.g. `provider_specific_data.environment`), and exclude sandbox orders from overview and transactions.

Change the deploy guide so the sandbox test uses a test-only offer/course and is done before the store is announced.

findings.title: Partial refunds of any size keep access, and admin views still show the order as fully paid
findings.description:
A `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED` event revokes access only when PayPal reports the capture as fully `REFUNDED`. Any partial refund, even 12.49 of 12.50, only appends a note to `order.raw.partial_refunds`. The buyer keeps access, and the admin dashboard does not show the refund: stats.py:118 reports `amount_refunded` only for `refunded` orders, and customers/overview count the full amount.

So a buyer who gets nearly all their money back (a partial refund by mistake, or a dispute settled for less than the full amount) keeps the course, and revenue in the dashboard is overstated. The spec does choose to keep access on partial refunds, but the money is not reconciled anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a running `refunded_amount` on the order (from the refund events, or from GET capture `seller_receivable_breakdown`). Show it in transactions, customers and overview. Then either revoke above a threshold (e.g. refunded >= 50%, or net below the offer minimum), or show a 'partially refunded, review access' flag to the admin.

findings.title: Unlisted offers can be bought by sequential numeric id, and the order status reveals their name, price and content
findings.description:
The public offer reads and `by-resource` hide offers with `is_publicly_listed=False`. `start_checkout`, however, resolves `offer_ref` with `get_offer_by_ref`, which accepts a small sequential integer id (common.py:198-199) and checks only `archived`.

Any signed-in user can therefore enumerate `POST /payments/1/offers/{1..N}/checkout` and buy a private or discounted offer covering a paid course (for example a 1 USD scholarship offer). `GET /orders/{uuid}` then reveals `offer_name`, `amount` and `resources`. The dashboard has no listing toggle yet, so this only matters for offers made through the API, but nothing on the server enforces 'unlisted = private'.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept only `offer_uuid` (not the numeric id) for public and checkout refs. If unlisted offers are meant for link holders only, also require the uuid for them explicitly. If they are meant to be private, refuse checkout for unlisted offers unless the caller is allowed (e.g. a usergroup or coupon check).

findings.title: Refund and chargeback revocation depends entirely on the webhook, which is optional in config and never backed by reconciliation
findings.description:
Access is revoked only in `_handle_event` (`capture_refunded` / `capture_reversed`). Reconciliation looks only at `created`/`approved`/`pending` orders and never re-checks `paid` ones.

`webhook_id` is optional: `_validate` checks only client_id and secret, and the UI labels it "opcional, recomendado" with "Sin webhook (recomendado configurarlo)". Without it, `handle_webhook` raises `WebhookVerificationError` and every event answers 400.

A buyer who gets a refund or wins a dispute in PayPal therefore keeps permanent access, and the dashboard still shows the sale as paid. The deploy guide does configure the webhook, but the platform shows the setup as finished without it, with no warning that refunds won't be enforced.
findings.evidence:
- reconcile.py:74-88: the query only selects status in ('created','approved') or 'pending'.
- paypal.py:465-467: `if not webhook_id: raise WebhookVerificationError("PayPal webhook_id is not configured")`
- configs.py:113-128: `_validate` sets `active=True` without a webhook_id.
- commerce.es.json: "optional_recommended": "opcional, recomendado".
findings.suggested_fix: Make `webhook_id` required to activate a live config, or show a blocking warning that refunds will not revoke access. Add a daily reconciliation pass over orders paid in the last ~180 days that GETs the capture and revokes on REFUNDED/REVERSED (rate-limited), so a lost or never-configured webhook cannot leave refunded buyers with access.

findings.title: Unauthenticated webhook endpoint makes an outbound PayPal verify call for every forged request (no rate limit)
findings.description:
`POST /payments/webhooks/paypal/1` needs no auth. Any body with the five `paypal-*` headers and an `id` makes the API call PayPal's `/v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature` (after an OAuth token), with a 20 s timeout. There is no rate limit on this route, no global limiter in app.py or src/core/middleware, and none in the Caddy config.

An attacker can flood it to use up API workers and outbound connections, and to burn the merchant app's PayPal rate limit. PayPal 429s on capture or verify then make real buyers' captures fail (502) and real webhooks answer 503.
findings.evidence: 5 forged POSTs with fake headers -> 5 x (400, {'detail': 'Invalid webhook signature'}) in 10.33 s. The paypal-mock log shows one `POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature` per forged request, from the api container (172.21.0.5).

verdicts.title: Buyer can be charged twice for one offer (second checkout while a capture is pending; concurrent captures of two approved orders)
verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute it. (a) `_user_owns_offer` (checkout.py:207-223) only counts enrollments in ACCESS_STATUSES = ('active','completed') (access.py:44). While order 1 is `pending`, its enrollment is `pending`, so `start_checkout` lets the buyer open a second order on the same enrollment row (lines 285-302). `_owned_through_other_order` at capture time sees no granting enrollment, so it captures. Later the `capture_completed` webhook (lines 641-661) or reconciliation (`refresh_order` -> `_record` -> `fulfill_order`) fulfills order 1 with no duplicate check. That check would not help anyway, because the money is already captured. The scenario is realistic: AccessReason has no 'pending' value, so the paywall shows the buy button again while PayPal reviews the payment. Reviews are common for new Business accounts, unaccepted currency and eCheck, and despliegue.md 7.1 itself mentions 'pendientes'. (b) `_capture_lock` is keyed on order_uuid only, and `_owned_through_other_order` runs before `provider.confirm` without any (user, offer)-wide lock. Two approved orders confirmed at the same time both pass the check and both capture. (b) needs two approved PayPal orders inside a capture window of about 1-2 s, so it is less likely than (a).
verdicts.evidence: The DB confirms the auditor's live runs (sc_pay_order). User 11 (audit_erin): orders 24 (95a816c8, capture TZZJCNNY4HZ1NXIYY) and 25 (0263f7a5, capture WP2SFBJ37X2JEZOGP) are both 'paid' 12.50 on the same enrollment 11. User 9 (carol) and user 10 (dave) each have two orders with distinct capture ids on one enrollment. Code: checkout.py:281 `if await _user_owns_offer(...)`, which ignores pending enrollments. checkout.py:425 `async with _capture_lock(order.order_uuid)` is a per-order lock. checkout.py:641-661 fulfills a completed capture with no ownership or duplicate check.
verdicts.fix: 1) In start_checkout, after the ALREADY_OWNED check, look for an order of the same (user_id, offer_id) with status 'pending', or 'approved' with update_date within ~30 min. If found, return 409 {code:'PAYMENT_PENDING', order_uuid} so the frontend sends the buyer to the existing order's status page. Add a 'pending' access reason, or a flag in GET /access, so the paywall shows 'Tu pago está en revisión' instead of the buy button. 2) Key the capture lock on the pair: `_capture_lock(f"{order.user_id}:{order.offer_id}")` (Redis key sc_pay:capture_lock:{user}:{offer} plus the local asyncio lock under the same key), held across `_owned_through_other_order` and `provider.confirm`. The ownership re-check then sees the first capture's fulfillment. 3) In fulfill_order, when the enrollment is already active and `provider_specific_data.order_uuid` names another order in PAID_STATUSES, still mark the new order paid (the money moved). Set `raw.duplicate_of = <granting order_uuid>`, do not overwrite order_uuid, and surface 'Cobro duplicado: reembolsar' in transactions/overview so the admin refunds it.

verdicts.title: Refunding the duplicate charge revokes access although another order for the same enrollment is still paid
verdicts.reasoning: This is confirmed in the DB and in the code. fulfill_order (fulfillment.py:354-367) overwrites enrollment.provider_specific_data.order_uuid with whichever order was fulfilled last. revoke_order (line 464) revokes when that order is refunded and never checks whether a sibling order on the same enrollment_id is still paid. The usergroup cleanup keys on enrollment status, so it follows the same wrong decision. It only happens after the double charge above, but refunding one of two charges is the natural admin response, with about a 50% chance of picking the granting order. The router has no admin grant/restore endpoint, so the paying buyer stays locked out until someone fixes the DB, or pays a third time.
verdicts.evidence: DB: user 10 (dave) has order 22 (30741270) 'refunded' and order 23 (bb9a20b9) 'paid', while enrollment 10 is 'refunded' with order_uuid=30741270. That is a paid, unrefunded order with no access. In the control case, user 9 (carol) had the non-granting order 21 refunded, and enrollment 9 stays 'active' with order_uuid=cd4e8bd2 (order 20). Code: fulfillment.py:464 `if data.get("order_uuid") in (None, order.order_uuid) and enrollment.status in ACCESS_STATUSES: enrollment.status = "refunded"`.
verdicts.fix: In revoke_order, after locking the enrollment, query `select PaymentsOrder where enrollment_id == order.enrollment_id and id != order.id and status in PAID_STATUSES order by paid_at desc`. If a row exists, keep enrollment.status 'active', set data.order_uuid/provider_capture_id/paid_at to that order's values, and skip the usergroup removal. Only revoke when no sibling paid order remains. Combined with the duplicate marking in fulfill_order (do not overwrite order_uuid), the granting order then stays stable.

verdicts.title: Sandbox PayPal configuration is accepted in production and grants permanent real access
verdicts.reasoning: The behaviour is real. configs.py:95-102 accepts 'sandbox' (and defaults to it) with no development_mode check. checkout_providers and start_checkout use any active config. Orders and enrollments do not record the environment. Anyone could complete a sandbox checkout with a free developer sandbox account, or with PayPal's generated test cards via 'Pagar con tarjeta', and get a permanent 'active' enrollment that counts as a sale. The anonymous providers endpoint advertises environment 'sandbox'. Severity is lower than reported: exploiting it needs an operator misconfiguration or the short pre-launch test window in despliegue.md 7.3, and the admin dashboard labels the active config '(sandbox)' (dash/payments/[subpage]/page.tsx:145; PaymentsConfigurationPage.tsx:181). The real gap is that nothing stops checkout for the public in sandbox on a production instance, and sandbox sales cannot be told apart afterwards.
verdicts.evidence: GET /api/v1/payments/1/checkout/providers (anonymous) -> [{"provider":"paypal",...,"environment":"sandbox",...}] (reproduced). configs.py:22 `ENVIRONMENTS = ("sandbox", "live")`, configs.py:102 `settings.setdefault("environment", "sandbox")`, and no use of is_development_mode in configs.py. The sc_pay_order model has no environment column. despliegue.md:158 tells Hilda to buy 'una oferta' in sandbox on the production platform.
verdicts.fix: In start_checkout, when `not is_development_mode()` and the config environment is not 'live', allow checkout only for org admins/maintainers (`_is_org_admin`) and answer 403 'La tienda está en modo de pruebas' for everyone else. Expose `test_mode: true` in checkout_providers so the frontend shows a banner. Write `environment` into order.raw and enrollment.provider_specific_data at checkout/fulfillment, and exclude non-live orders from overview/transactions/customers, or tag them. Update despliegue.md 7.3 to run the sandbox test on a throwaway offer/course and archive it before switching to live.

verdicts.title: Partial refunds keep access and the admin views still show the order as fully paid
verdicts.reasoning: The behaviour is accurate (order 19 has raw.partial_refunds [{amount '12.49'}]), but it is the documented design, not a vulnerability. spec-tecnica.md:96 says to revoke 'solo si la captura quedó REFUNDED, no si es parcial'. A buyer cannot trigger a partial refund: the merchant issues it, or agrees to it as a partial dispute settlement. Buyer-initiated chargebacks arrive as PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REVERSED, which revokes. Keeping access is therefore the merchant's own choice. The only effect is reporting accuracy: transactions and customers ignore partial refund amounts. That is a minor dashboard bookkeeping issue and does not open an access or money path.
verdicts.evidence: checkout.py:683-699: revoke only when get_capture_status == 'REFUNDED', otherwise append to raw.partial_refunds. spec-tecnica.md:96 mandates exactly this. DB order 19 (audit_bob) shows the partial note, then full refund -> 'refunded'.
verdicts.fix: Optional, non-security: keep a `refunded_amount` on the order (sum of refund events, or from GET capture seller_receivable_breakdown.total_refunded_amount), show it in transactions/customers and net it out of the overview revenue, and add a 'Reembolso parcial' badge so Hilda can decide on access manually.

verdicts.title: Unlisted offers can be bought by sequential numeric id
verdicts.reasoning: The code does let start_checkout resolve any non-archived offer by numeric id without checking is_publicly_listed (common.py:192-205, checkout.py:248). It does not matter in this deployment. The admin UI has no listing toggle: no web component or service references is_publicly_listed, and offers are created with the default True. The only path to an unlisted offer is archive_offer, which also sets archived=True, and archived offers are refused at checkout (404). The only unlisted offer in the dev DB (id 3) is archived. An unlisted-but-active offer can only be created by an admin calling the raw API, and the spec gives unlisted no 'private' meaning; it only removes the offer from the catalog. This is a latent hardening item, not an exploitable issue.
verdicts.evidence: grep finds is_publicly_listed only in api/src (offers.py, models, demo sync), with zero hits in web/components, web/app or web/services. offers.py:294 sets is_publicly_listed=False only together with archived=True. DB sc_pay_offer: id 3 is_publicly_listed=f, archived=t. ids 1 and 2 are listed.
verdicts.fix: Hardening (optional): in start_checkout, refuse offers with is_publicly_listed=False unless `offer_ref` equals offer.offer_uuid (link-holder semantics) or the caller is an org admin. Prefer uuid-only refs for the public checkout route.

verdicts.title: Refund/chargeback revocation depends entirely on the webhook, which is optional and never backed by reconciliation
verdicts.reasoning: This is confirmed as a defense-in-depth gap. Revocation happens only in _handle_event (capture_refunded/capture_reversed). reconcile_once only selects created/approved/pending orders (reconcile.py:74-88). handle_webhook rejects every event when webhook_id is empty (paypal.py:465-467). `_validate` activates the config without a webhook_id, and the UI calls it optional ('opcional, recomendado', 'Sin webhook (recomendado configurarlo)'). A buyer who wins a card chargeback (REVERSED) on a store without a webhook keeps permanent access. Mitigations that lower the severity: despliegue.md 7.1/7.2 and the checklist (line 246) require creating the webhook and pasting its ID. When configured, PayPal redelivers failed webhooks for days, and handle_provider_webhook answers 503 on transient errors. A non-transient processing exception answers 2xx and is never retried, though, and reconciliation will not heal it.
verdicts.evidence: reconcile.py:74-88 (no paid-order pass). paypal.py:465-467 `if not webhook_id: raise WebhookVerificationError(...)`. configs.py:113-128 sets active=True with only client_id and secret. web/locales-sc/commerce.es.json:90,96 show the 'Sin webhook (recomendado configurarlo)' and 'opcional, recomendado' labels.
verdicts.fix: 1) When saving a config with environment 'live' and no webhook_id, refuse it (400 'Falta el Webhook ID: sin él los reembolsos no retiran el acceso'), or at least keep a blocking warning state on the card. 2) Add a low-frequency reconciliation pass (e.g. daily, Redis-locked) over orders with status in PAID_STATUSES and paid_at within the last 180 days. Call provider.get_capture_status(cfg, order.provider_capture_id), throttled to a few per second, and call revoke_order on 'REFUNDED' or 'REVERSED'. Partial refunds keep the current rule. 3) Mark webhook events that finished 'failed' for re-processing by the same pass.

verdicts.title: Unauthenticated webhook endpoint makes an outbound PayPal verify call for every forged request (no rate limit)
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. Any POST with the five paypal-* headers and a JSON body with an id reaches `_call(... '/v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature')` (paypal.py:463-492). The OAuth token is cached, so the cost is one outbound call per request. Nothing limits the route: no `_check_rate` on it (the router uses _check_rate only for checkout at line 234), no global limiter in app.py or src/core, and none in deploy/caddy/Caddyfile. The handler is async, so it does not pin worker threads, and the amplification is only 1:1. The real risk is an attacker driving PayPal to throttle (429) the merchant's API credentials or server IP, which would make real captures and verifications fail. Cheap header checks (cert-url host, transmission-time window, auth-algo) only stop naive floods because they are forgeable; a rate limit is the effective control.
verdicts.evidence: A POST without the paypal headers returns 400 cheaply, so the pre-check exists only for header presence. With headers, every request triggers a verify call: the auditor's mock log showed one verify call per forged request. grep for rate_limit/slowapi in app.py and src/core returns nothing, and payments.py:94-105 has no rate check.
verdicts.fix: In api_provider_webhook, call `_check_rate(f"sc_pay_webhook:{client_ip}", 120, 60)` before the service call (client IP from X-Forwarded-For as set by Caddy), and add a global per-org cap (e.g. `sc_pay_webhook_org:{org_id}` 600/min). In PayPalProvider.handle_webhook, before the remote verify, reject when auth_algo != 'SHA256withRSA', when the cert_url host is not api.paypal.com/api.sandbox.paypal.com (matching the config environment), or when transmission_time is more than about 15 minutes from now. Optionally verify the signature locally against a cached PayPal cert (CRC32 of the raw body), so forged requests never leave the server.

checked_ok: Paywall read paths, tested live as an anonymous user and as a signed-in non-buyer (audit_mallory, id 7) on both paid courses (course 3 text, course 4 video). None leaked content: /courses/{uuid}, /meta?slim=false (also with with_unpublished_activities=true, which is downgraded for non-editors), /chapters/course/{uuid}/meta, /chapters/{id}, /chapters/course/{id}/page/1/limit/10, /activities/{uuid}, /activities/id/{id} and /activities/chapter/{id} all return content {"paid_access":false} with details null.

Media and files: /stream/video and /content/.../activities/... video and PDF answer 402. The content router resolves the canonical path before checking access, enforces course-in-org and activity-in-course, and serves only thumbnails and course-root files publicly. Production uses filesystem delivery, so every byte goes through the gate (no long-lived presigned URLs).

Editor-only reads (/editor-bootstrap, /versions, /state, /export) answer 403 for non-editors. Search returns no activity text. RAG retrieval runs check_ee_activity_paid_access on every chunk. The AI quiz/scenario routes require course UPDATE. Assignment reads run the activity gate for sessions.

Progress and trail: PUT /progress/activity answers 402 for unpaid callers, as do POST /trail/add_course (402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED) and /trail/add_activity. GET progress returns only the caller's own rows.

Chapter/activity reorder rejects activities and chapters from other courses, so a paid activity cannot be linked into a free course's tree. Contributor applications are created PENDING, so they don't unlock access.

Access cache: refund and revoke bump the Redis access version. After the full refund of bob's order, /access, the activity read and the stream were denied immediately. The anonymous /meta cache stores only the anonymous, scrubbed view and is invalidated by pricing_changed. In theory a request that started while the course was still free could write a stale unscrubbed view right after an offer is created (60 s TTL); I did not reproduce it.
Order IDOR: another signed-in user gets 404 on GET, capture and cancel of someone else's order. Anonymous capture works by spec (the uuid is the secret) and only completes the owner's own payment.

Admin endpoints (/customers, /config, /overview, /transactions, /offers, /groups) answer 403 for a regular member. API tokens are refused on payments admin and checkout. Config responses never include the secret (has_secret only); the secret is Fernet-encrypted.
redirect_uri open-redirect guard rejects evil.example, cursos.sanarycriarve.com.evil.example, userinfo@ tricks and javascript: (400). The archived offer (id 3) cannot be checked out (404).

Amount, currency and custom_id: the order amount always comes from the DB. evaluate_order and the capture_completed webhook both require Decimal amount == order.amount, the same currency, custom_id == order_uuid and the PayPal order id. A mismatch is recorded as failed and never grants access. customer_choice has no effect: the price stays fixed.

Forged webhooks with fake headers answer 400. Event ids are deduplicated through a unique insert (done or in-flight events are skipped). A refunded order is never resurrected by a late COMPLETED event (fulfill_order skips refunded orders). A partial refund followed by the rest of the refund revokes access correctly.
Production .env.example has DEVELOPMENT_MODE=false, so the LEARNHOUSE_PAYPAL_API_BASE/WEB_BASE overrides and localhost redirects are ignored there.

Constraints and test data:

findings.title: Open redirect in the Sanar y Criar proxy bounce for signed-in visitors: /login?redirect=/..//evil.com sends them off-site
findings.description: signedInAuthRedirect() (new Sanar y Criar code) checks ?redirect / ?next with safeInternalPath() and passes the RAW string to new URL(target, req.url). safeInternalPath (services/security/url.ts:20-31) only rejects values that start with '//' and checks the origin after parsing against a dummy base. It never looks at the normalized pathname. A value with dot segments such as '/..//evil.com', '/./%2Fevil.com' or '/a/..//evil.com' passes: it starts with '/' and resolves to the dummy origin. But it normalizes to the pathname '//evil.com', so new URL() gives 'http://host//evil.com', and Next emits a Location header pointing at evil.com. Anyone holding the LH_session marker cookie (set on every login) who opens a crafted link on the real domain, e.g. https://cursos.sanarycriarve.com/login?redirect=/..//evil.com, is sent straight to the attacker's site (307) with no click needed. That is a good setup for a fake 'your session expired, log in again' or 'complete your payment' phishing page. safeRedirectPath() in components/Payments/commerce.ts:131 relies on the same guard, so withRedirect()/useAuthRedirectHref() also carry such values unchanged into the login and signup links. On the client side, the Next router itself stays same-origin (tested).
findings.evidence: curl --cookie 'LH_session=1' 'http://localhost:3200/login?redirect=/..//evil.com'  -> HTTP/1.1 307, location: http://evil.com/ (also '/.%2F%2Fevil.com', '/./%2Fevil.com', '/a/..//evil.com' -> location: http://evil.com/). Controls held: '//evil.com', '/\evil.com', '/%09/evil.com', 'https://evil.com' -> /home. Headless Chrome (isolated profile, cookie LH_session=1): http://localhost:3200/login?redirect=/..//example.invalid/phish => document requests ["http://localhost:3200/login?redirect=/..//example.invalid/phish","http://example.invalid/phish"]. node: new URL('/..//evil.com','http://localhost:3200/login').href === 'http://localhost:3200//evil.com'; new URL('/.//evil.com','https://relative.invalid/').origin === 'https://relative.invalid' (so the guard accepts it).
findings.suggested_fix: In safeInternalPath, return the normalized form instead of the raw input: const u = new URL(value, RELATIVE_BASE); if (u.origin !== base origin || u.pathname.startsWith('//')) return fallback; return u.pathname + u.search + u.hash. Optionally also reject any '/.' or '/..' segment up front. That fixes proxy.ts:193, commerce.ts safeRedirectPath and getUriWithOrg together. Add '/..//x', '/./%2Fx' and '/a/..//x' to tests/sc-fixes.test.mjs.

findings.title: Unauthenticated open redirect at /redirect_from_auth?next=/..//evil, also reached after every login/signup through ?redirect
findings.description: Upstream code that ships in this fork, not a Sanar y Criar change, but the new buyer flows (offer/course -> /signup?redirect=... -> /login?redirect=...) now route every buyer through it. The handler compares the origin of new URL(rawNext, baseOrigin), then rebuilds dest from candidate.pathname. For '/..//evil.com' that pathname is the normalized '//evil.com', and new URL('//evil.com', base) is a protocol-relative URL to evil.com. No session is needed. In addition, buildCallbackUrl() in login.tsx:151, OpenSignup.tsx:154 and InviteOnlySignUp.tsx:141 lets '/..//evil.com' through its /^\/(?!\/)/ test and forwards it as ?next to /redirect_from_auth. So https://cursos.sanarycriarve.com/login?redirect=/..//evil.com shows the real login page and, after a successful password, Google or 2FA login (window.location.href = callbackUrl), lands the buyer on the attacker's site. Same after signup.
findings.evidence: curl 'http://localhost:3200/redirect_from_auth?next=%2F..%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx' (no cookies) -> HTTP/1.1 307, location: http://evil.example/x ; curl 'http://localhost:3200/redirect_from_auth?next=/./%2Fevil.example' -> location: http://evil.example/ . Headless Chrome: http://localhost:3200/redirect_from_auth?next=%2F..%2F%2Fexample.invalid%2Fphish => [..., "http://example.invalid/phish"]. Code: proxy.ts:528-531 `const candidate = new URL(rawNext, baseOrigin); if (candidate.origin === baseOrigin) { dest = `${candidate.pathname}${candidate.search}${candidate.hash}` }` then `new URL(dest, base)`; login.tsx:151 `const dest = raw && /^\/(?!\/)/.test(raw) ? raw : '/home'`.
findings.suggested_fix: In redirect_from_auth, after the origin check, collapse leading slashes (dest = '/' + candidate.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '') + search + hash), or fall back to '/' when candidate.pathname starts with '//'. Replace the three buildCallbackUrl regexes with the fixed safeInternalPath(raw, '/home'). Mark the edits 'Sanar y Criar:' since they touch upstream code.

verdicts.title: Open redirect in the Sanar y Criar proxy bounce for signed-in visitors: /login?redirect=/..//evil.com sends them off-site
verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute this one. safeInternalPath (services/security/url.ts:20-31) only rejects raw values that start with '//', contain a backslash or contain control characters. It then checks the origin of the parsed URL and returns the RAW value, never the normalized pathname. '/..//evil.com' starts with a single '/' and resolves same-origin against the dummy base, so it passes. signedInAuthRedirect (proxy.ts:193-201) then calls new URL(target, req.url), which normalizes the dot segments to the pathname '//evil.com'. Next writes that same-origin URL as the relative Location '//evil.com', and the browser reads it as a protocol-relative URL to evil.com. The '/./%2Fevil.com' variant works because searchParams.get() decodes %2F into '/', which gives '/.//evil.com'. The only precondition is the LH_session marker cookie, which any signed-in visitor has (or anyone who sets it, since only its presence is checked). No click is needed, so a link on the real domain sends the visitor to a phishing page. A reverse proxy does not normalize the query string, so this also holds in production. commerce.ts safeRedirectPath and withRedirect use the same guard, so the payload also travels into signup and login links, and from there into finding 2.
verdicts.evidence: Reproduced against localhost:3200 with cookie LH_session=1: '/login?redirect=/..//evil.com' -> 307 location: http://evil.com/; '/login?redirect=/a/..//evil.com' -> 307 location: http://evil.com/; '/login?redirect=/./%2Fevil.com' -> 307 location: http://evil.com/. Control: '/login?redirect=//evil.com' -> location: /home. node: new URL('/..//evil.com','http://localhost:3200/login').href === 'http://localhost:3200//evil.com'. Code: url.ts:25-27 returns `value` (raw) after only an origin check.
verdicts.fix: In services/security/url.ts safeInternalPath, return the normalized form and reject a normalized pathname that starts with '//': `const u = new URL(value, RELATIVE_BASE); if (u.origin !== new URL(RELATIVE_BASE).origin || u.pathname.startsWith('//')) return fallback; return u.pathname + u.search + u.hash`. This one change also fixes proxy.ts signedInAuthRedirect, commerce.ts safeRedirectPath/withRedirect/redirectFromSearch and the other callers. Add regression cases '/..//x', '/a/..//x', '/.//x' and '/./%2Fx' (the decoded form) to tests/sc-fixes.test.mjs, each expecting the fallback.

verdicts.title: Unauthenticated open redirect at /redirect_from_auth?next=/..//evil, also reached after every login/signup through ?redirect
verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute this one either. proxy.ts:526-531 checks the origin of new URL(rawNext, baseOrigin) and then rebuilds dest from candidate.pathname. That pathname is already normalized to '//evil.example/x', and new URL(dest, base) at line 537 treats it as protocol-relative, which gives an off-site Location. No session is needed. buildCallbackUrl in app/auth/login/login.tsx:151 uses /^\/(?!\/)/, which accepts '/..//evil.com', and forwards it as ?next. After the password is accepted, the code runs window.location.href = callbackUrl (login.tsx about line 448); the Google signIn callbackUrl and the MFA callbackUrl carry the same value. OpenSignup.tsx:151 and InviteOnlySignUp.tsx:138 define the same buildCallbackUrl. So a crafted /login?redirect=/..//evil.com link shows the real login page and, after a successful login, sends the user to the attacker's site. That is a credible way to phish a 'payment failed, re-enter details' step. The code is upstream, but it ships in this fork and the new buyer flows route through it.
verdicts.evidence: Reproduced without cookies: '/redirect_from_auth?next=%2F..%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx' -> 307 location: http://evil.example/x; '/redirect_from_auth?next=/./%2Fevil.example' -> 307 location: http://evil.example/. Control: '?next=//evil.example' -> location: /. node: new URL('//evil.com','http://localhost:3200/').href === 'http://evil.com/'. Code: proxy.ts:528-530 `const candidate = new URL(rawNext, baseOrigin); if (candidate.origin === baseOrigin) { dest = `${candidate.pathname}...` }` then `new URL(dest, base)`; login.tsx:151 `const dest = raw && /^\/(?!\/)/.test(raw) ? raw : '/home'`.
verdicts.fix: In proxy.ts redirect_from_auth (mark it 'Sanar y Criar:'), set dest only when `candidate.origin === baseOrigin && !candidate.pathname.startsWith('//')`, and otherwise keep '/'. Alternatively collapse the leading slashes: dest = '/' + candidate.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '') + candidate.search + candidate.hash. In login.tsx, OpenSignup.tsx and InviteOnlySignUp.tsx buildCallbackUrl (mark them 'Sanar y Criar:'), replace the regex with the fixed safeInternalPath(raw, '/home') from finding 1, so that both the client and the proxy layer reject dot-segment payloads.

checked_ok: API checkout redirect_uri guard (services/payments/checkout.py is_allowed_redirect): https://evil.com/, http://localhost:3200@evil.com/, http://evil.com#@localhost:3200/, http://evil.com\@localhost:3200/, http://localhost:3200.evil.com/, //evil.com/, javascript://localhost:3200/%0aalert(1) -> 400 'redirect_uri no permitido'. Prod .env.example pins LEARNHOUSE_DOMAIN/FRONTEND_DOMAIN to cursos.sanarycriarve.com with SSL=true and DEVELOPMENT_MODE=false, so the dev-only allowance (any localhost/127.0.0.1 port, confirmed working in dev) does not apply in production. Note: the probe left 4 test orders in 'created' status for alumna.api.webhook in the dev DB.
checkout_url handling: offer-detail.tsx only follows it through safeExternalUrl (http/https, no userinfo) and window.location.assign; it is the only consumer of startOfferCheckout/checkout_url.

Proxy bounce with the usual payloads (//evil.com, /%2F%2Fevil.com, /\evil.com, %2F%2Fevil.com, /%09/evil.com, https://evil.com, /%5Cevil.com) -> /home; /login and /%6cogin as the target -> /home (loop guard works).

Client-side sinks: router.replace(currentAuthRedirect()) in login.tsx and router.push(getUriWithOrg(slug, currentAuthRedirect())) in signup.tsx. Tested in headless Chrome: the Next app router given '/..//example.invalid/x' stays same-origin (http://localhost:3200/example.invalid/x).

CSRF: POST payments/1/offers/<id>/checkout and PUT progress/activity/<id> with cookie auth and Origin https://evil.com or null -> 403 'CSRF validation failed: Origin not allowed'. With the right Origin the request goes through. Without Origin it passes, but browsers always send Origin on cross-site POST/PUT.

Return-URL auto actions on the offer page: ?checkout=return&order=<uuid> runs capture with the viewer's token, but the API returns 404 when the signed-in user is not the order owner. ?checkout=cancelled cancels only orders the caller owns (user_id check). Order uuids are UUIDv4.

Server-side authZ for dashboard data: as a buyer, payments/1/config, /overview, /transactions, /customers and /offers -> 403. Admin config response returns has_secret plus webhook_id/client_id, never client_secret. checkout/providers exposes only public data (client_id, methods, currencies).
Paywall is enforced on the server: an anonymous GET activities/<paid activity> returns content {paid_access:false}, and the anonymous course meta does not include the paid text.

CORS: the main policy is pinned to the configured host plus localhost; evil.com gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. ExtraOriginsCORSMiddleware gives the extra origins only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS with safelisted headers, removes Access-Control-Allow-Credentials (test_reconcile_cors.py asserts this), and extra origins are not in the CSRF allowlist.

Clickjacking: /store/offers/<id> returns X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP frame-ancestors 'none'. Course routes allow SAMEORIGIN only. The upstream /embed route (frame-ancestors *) has no checkout and the store page refuses framing.

XSS: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML in the Sanar y Criar components, store, auth or footer/menu files. Thumbnails go through safeImageSrc plus cssUrl (JSON-quoted, set via React style/CSSOM). Receipt links go through safeExternalUrl. Resource links are built from uuids via getUriWithOrg. PayPal dashboard links are hard-coded. course.tsx learning.link is upstream and unchanged, and React 19.3 blocks javascript: hrefs.

Token handling: progress saves send the bearer token in the Authorization header (fetch with keepalive), never in the URL. localStorage holds only progress positions, the language flag and UI prefs. The new services/payments server actions do not log tokens, and URLs use encodeURIComponent on the API base.
Error messages: buyer-facing checkout/capture errors are fixed Spanish strings. ProviderError text goes only to the logs and the webhook-event table, never into responses.

findings.title: actualizar.sh skips the pre-update backup AND the Alembic migrations when the db service is stopped or not answering yet
findings.description: The script decides whether the database already exists only if the `db` container is running AND `psql` answers. If db is stopped (for example after `docker compose down`/`stop` for maintenance), or is running but still in startup or recovery so psql fails and `|| echo 0` kicks in, `db_existente` stays false. The script then treats a production database with real data as a first deploy: no `backup.sh --solo-db`, no `alembic upgrade heads`, and the new image starts directly. The app never runs Alembic at boot, only `SQLModel.metadata.create_all` (src/core/events/database.py:398). So the new code runs on the old schema, and create_all adds the new version's tables outside Alembic. Later `upgrade heads` runs then fail with 'relation already exists'. restaurar.sh's own comment describes this exact breakage. Step 5 does not catch it: `alembic current` returns the old revision (not empty), so the script prints 'Listo'.
findings.evidence:
actualizar.sh:63-74
  db_existente=false
  if servicio_corriendo db; then
    tablas="$(dc exec -T db psql ... 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [[ "${tablas//[^0-9]/}" -gt 0 ]] && db_existente=true
  fi
  ... else info "1/5 Base de datos vacía o detenida: no hace falta copia"
actualizar.sh:118-119  else info "3/5 Primer despliegue: el primer arranque crea las tablas"
actualizar.sh:124      dc up -d --remove-orphans
restaurar.sh comment: "the newer image would add its tables with create_all and break later migrations."
apps/api/src/core/events/database.py:398  await conn.run_sync(SQLModel.metadata.create_all)  (no alembic at boot)
findings.suggested_fix: Always run `dc up -d --no-recreate db redis` and `esperar_sano db 120` BEFORE detecting the database. Fail hard if psql errors; never fall back to 0. Only treat the DB as new when the query succeeds and returns 0. Also, after first deploy, refuse to continue with an unmigrated DB if `alembic current` is non-empty but differs from the new image's heads.

findings.title: PayPal sandbox mode on the production platform lets anyone get paid courses with fake money, and those grants survive the switch to live
findings.description: The go-live guide (7.3.1) says to configure the production platform with Entorno: Pruebas (sandbox) and buy an offer. sandbox is also the default whenever environment is missing. While that config is active, every listed offer on cursos.sanarycriarve.com can be checked out against api-m.sandbox.paypal.com. Anyone can pay with a free PayPal developer sandbox account or a public sandbox test card through the 'Pagar con tarjeta' option. The server grants real access because the capture is COMPLETED and amount, currency and custom_id match. Orders do not record which PayPal environment paid them. So after the switch to live, those enrollments stay, revenue stats include fake sales, and reconciliation and refunds never revisit them. No backend or checkout guard blocks a sandbox config when development_mode is false. The only hint is a dashboard label.

findings.title: Any unauthenticated request to cursos.* may carry a 6 GB body, and the internal nginx buffers it to disk: easy disk-exhaustion DoS of the single VPS
findings.description: Caddy sets `request_body max_size 6GB` for the whole cursos.sanarycriarve.com site. The image's nginx sets `client_max_body_size 6G` server-wide and leaves proxy_request_buffering at its default (on), with client_body_buffer_size 32k. So nginx writes each body to a temp file in the container's writable layer (/var/lib/docker on the host disk) before the API sees the request or checks auth. A few parallel anonymous POSTs to any path fill the disk (for example /api/v1/payments/webhooks/paypal/1, or any 404 path under /api/v1). Postgres, Redis AOF, HLS output and backups share that disk (80 GB VPS). Large bodies are only needed for admin video/PDF uploads. LearnHouse has no chunked upload, but those are still a handful of endpoints.
findings.suggested_fix: In Caddy, set a small default (for example `request_body { max_size 50MB }`) and allow 6GB only on the upload routes (a path matcher for the activity/video/document upload endpoints), or check auth first with forward_auth. In nginx (Sanar y Criar edit), move `client_max_body_size 6G` into the upload locations and set `proxy_request_buffering off` there so bodies stream to the API instead of filling disk.

findings.title: Off-site backups upload the .env secrets together with the full database, unencrypted and never pruned
findings.description: With SC_BACKUP_RCLONE_REMOTE set, which the guide asks for, each nightly folder goes to the remote as is: env.respaldo, db.dump and content.tar.gz. env.respaldo holds LEARNHOUSE_AUTH_JWT_SECRET_KEY, which is enough to forge an admin session. It also holds LEARNHOUSE_MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the Postgres password, the Resend key and the initial admin password. The Fernet key that encrypts the PayPal client secret in the DB is sha256(JWT secret). So anyone who reaches the remote (a Google Drive or B2 account takeover, a shared folder) can decrypt the live PayPal credentials and read every buyer's email, name and purchases. rclone `copy` has no client-side encryption unless the operator happens to configure a `crypt` remote, and the docs only say 'usa un destino privado'. Local retention (SC_BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS) never applies to the remote, so secrets and personal data pile up there forever, including the initial admin password the guide tells the admin to delete.

backup.sh:88  rclone copy "$destino" "$remoto/$sello"
backup.sh:79  find "$raiz" ... -mtime +"$dias" ... rm -rf   (local only)
apps/api/src/services/webhooks/crypto.py: _fernet_key(): secret = ...auth_jwt_secret_key; digest = hashlib.sha256(secret.encode()).digest()
despliegue.md:202 "La copia incluye .env (secretos): usa un destino privado."
findings.suggested_fix: Do not upload env.respaldo (keep secrets in the password manager, as the guide already says), or encrypt the whole folder before upload (`age`/`gpg` with a public key whose private key is off-server), or require a `crypt:` rclone remote. Add remote retention (`rclone delete --min-age ${dias}d`), or document bucket lifecycle rules.

findings.title: The documented daily backup cron line silently never runs until backups/ exists (first deploy never creates it)
findings.description: The cron entry redirects output to backups/backup.log before backup.sh runs. If ./backups does not exist, the shell fails the redirection and never runs the script. The first-deploy flow (actualizar.sh on an empty DB) skips backup.sh, so nothing creates backups/ until a later update or a manual run. If SC_BACKUP_DIR is set to an absolute path, backups/ is never created and the cron job never works. Cron output usually goes nowhere on a VPS without an MTA, so the operator sees no error and simply has no backups.

Also add a failure signal, for example a healthchecks.io ping or a 'last OK backup' age check in actualizar.sh.

findings.title: Fernet key for the stored PayPal secret is derived from the JWT secret: rotating it breaks payments, and leaking it exposes PayPal
findings.description: .env.example says changing LEARNHOUSE_AUTH_JWT_SECRET_KEY only closes all sessions. In fact the PayPal client secret is encrypted with sha256(JWT secret). Rotating the JWT secret, which is what you do after a suspected leak, makes credentials_from_config raise SECRET_UNREADABLE, and checkout, capture and reconciliation stop until the secret is re-entered. And a JWT-secret leak also exposes the PayPal live secret, so the incident response has to rotate it at PayPal too. Nothing documents this.

findings.title: nginx access log inside the container stores password-reset codes, emails and magic-link tokens, with no rotation
findings.description: The all-in-one image uses Alpine's nginx.conf, which writes `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main` to a regular file in the container's writable layer, not to stdout. So the compose json-file limits (10m x 5) do not apply. It grows until the container is recreated. Every full request line is logged, including `/reset?email=<buyer email>&resetCode=<code>`, `/auth/magic?token=<token>`, `/verify-email?token=...` and PayPal return URLs. Short-lived credentials and buyer emails sit in plaintext with no retention policy. HLS segment requests also add steady disk growth.

findings.title: Supply chain: CI actions and runtime base images use mutable tags while the job holds packages:write
findings.description: The image workflow has `packages: write` and logs into GHCR with GITHUB_TOKEN, but pins third-party actions by movable tags, not commit SHAs. A retagged or compromised action release could push a backdoored :sc-v* or :sanarycriar image that production then pulls. In production, actualizar.sh runs `docker compose pull` every time, and compose uses floating tags `caddy:2-alpine` and `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`. So every update silently takes whatever those tags point to that day, including the TLS edge with all traffic and the database, with no digest pin and no review.
findings.evidence:
sanarycriar-image.yml:24-26 permissions: contents: read / packages: write
:38 uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
:65 uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4.4.1
:68 uses: docker/login-action@v4.6.0
:75 uses: docker/build-push-action@v7.4.0
docker-compose.prod.yml:60 image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16 ; :109 image: caddy:2-alpine
actualizar.sh:110 dc pull
findings.suggested_fix: Pin actions to full commit SHAs (keep the version as a comment; Renovate is already configured upstream). In compose, pin caddy and pgvector to an exact version plus @sha256 digest (for example caddy:2.11.7-alpine@sha256:...), and optionally deploy SC_LMS_IMAGE by digest.

findings.title: Platform container runs every service as root and the app connects to Postgres as a superuser
findings.description: The final image stage has no USER, so pm2, Next.js, the FastAPI API (which runs ffmpeg/Pillow on uploaded files) and collab all run as uid 0. The `nextjs` user exists only in an intermediate stage. The compose file sets no `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]`, cap_drop or read_only. The API's connection string uses the `learnhouse` role, which the official Postgres image creates as SUPERUSER because it is POSTGRES_USER. Any SQL injection or app RCE therefore gets superuser on the DB (COPY ... TO PROGRAM runs commands in the db container) and root inside the app container, which holds the whole .env through env_file.
findings.evidence:
docker run --rm --entrypoint sh sanarycriar/lms:local -c id -> uid=0(root) gid=0(root)
docker/start.sh: pm2 start server-wrapper.js ... / pm2 start uv ... run app.py (no user switch)
docker-compose.prod.yml:35 LEARNHOUSE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING: postgresql://learnhouse:...@db:5432/learnhouse
docker-compose.prod.yml:63 POSTGRES_USER: learnhouse (superuser in the official image)
findings.suggested_fix: Add `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]` and `cap_drop: [ALL]` (add back only what nginx needs to bind :80, or move nginx to a high port). Create a non-superuser app role (owner of the learnhouse DB, NOSUPERUSER) through an init script, and keep the superuser only for backup/restore. Longer term, run pm2 services as a non-root user in the image.

findings.title: Full PayPal 'payer' object (PayPal email, name, payer_id) stored on every order row and therefore in every backup
findings.description: _trim() keeps `payer` and `purchase_units` from PayPal create, capture and status responses, and fulfillment merges them into sc_pay_order.raw. That stores the PayPal account holder's email and full name, which can be a third party such as a relative who paid, plus payer_id and country. This data is not needed for fulfillment, is not shown in the admin UI, and ends up in db.dump and any off-site copy. It goes against data minimisation for a psychology practice's customer base.

paypal.py:51 _MAX_RAW_KEYS = ("id", "status", "intent", "purchase_units", "payer", "links", "create_time", "update_time")
paypal.py:89-93 return {k: data[k] for k in _MAX_RAW_KEYS if k in data}
fulfillment.py:350 _merge_raw(order, result.raw, "capture"); :414 _merge_raw(order, result.raw, "last_status")
db/payments/payments.py:278 raw: dict = Field(... JSON ...)
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `payer` from _MAX_RAW_KEYS and strip `purchase_units[*].shipping` and `payee` before storing. Keep only ids, statuses, amounts and capture ids, which is all reconciliation needs.

verdicts.title: actualizar.sh skips the pre-update backup AND the Alembic migrations when the db service is stopped or not answering yet
verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute it. db_existente is only set when `servicio_corriendo db` is true AND psql returns a positive count. The `2>/dev/null || echo 0` fallback turns any psql failure (for example 'the database system is starting up' right after a reboot, or recovery) into 'empty DB'. A stopped db (after `docker compose stop` or `down`) skips detection entirely. Both cases skip backup.sh and `alembic upgrade heads`. Step 4 `dc up -d` then starts db plus the NEW image. The app never runs Alembic at boot (no alembic reference in app.py, docker-entrypoint.sh, docker/start.sh or src/core/events). database.py only runs `SQLModel.metadata.create_all`, which adds new tables but not new columns, so the new code runs on the old schema. Step 5 then only checks that `alembic current` is non-empty. It is (the old revision), so the script prints 'Listo'. The next `upgrade heads` hits tables create_all already made. restaurar.sh:93-94 documents this exact breakage. The operator has to run an update while db is down or starting, which happens: maintenance stop, or a reboot just before the update.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/scripts/actualizar.sh:63-68 (servicio_corriendo gate + `|| echo 0`), :72-73 skip backup, :118-119 skip migrations, :124 `dc up -d --remove-orphans`, :130-136 accepts any non-empty revision. apps/api/src/core/events/database.py:396-398 create_all only. restaurar.sh:93-94 comment.
verdicts.fix: In actualizar.sh, before detection: `dc up -d --no-recreate db redis` and `esperar_sano db 120 || fallar ...`. Then run the count query without the fallback: `tablas="$(dc exec -T db psql -U learnhouse -d learnhouse -Atc "select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'")" || fallar "No se pudo consultar la base de datos"`. Set db_existente=true only when the count is greater than 0. In step 5, also compare `alembic current` against `alembic heads` of the running image and fail when they differ.

verdicts.title: PayPal sandbox mode on the production platform lets anyone get paid courses with fake money, and those grants survive the switch to live
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed in code. configs.py:102 defaults environment to sandbox. paypal.py:100/139 use sandbox whenever the setting is missing or invalid. Nothing in checkout, fulfillment or reconcile blocks checkout with a sandbox config when development_mode is false. sc_pay_order has no environment or config-snapshot column (db/payments/payments.py:240-280), so sandbox-paid orders cannot be told apart later. despliegue.md 7.3.1 tells the operator to run the sandbox test on the production host. limpiar-datos-de-prueba.py only removes '(borrar)' offers and @example.com users, not sandbox orders. Impact is limited: the window is short (the go-live test), an outsider has to notice it and use a sandbox buyer account, and the loss is course access, not money. Downgraded to low.
verdicts.evidence: services/payments/configs.py:102 `settings.setdefault("environment", "sandbox")`; providers/paypal.py:100,139; db/payments/payments.py PaymentsOrder has no environment field; docs/despliegue.md:158 '**Primero en sandbox** ... configura la tarjeta con Entorno: Pruebas (sandbox). Compra una oferta'.
verdicts.fix: Change despliegue.md 7.3.1 so the sandbox test runs locally (dev stack) or on a staging host. If it must run on production, use only an unlisted '(borrar)' offer, keep real offers unlisted, and run limpiar-datos-de-prueba.py afterwards. In code: add `environment` to sc_pay_order at create time. In checkout.py, refuse to create orders for non-admin users when `not is_development_mode()` and the active config is sandbox.

verdicts.title: Any unauthenticated request to cursos.* may carry a 6 GB body, and the internal nginx buffers it to disk: easy disk-exhaustion DoS of the single VPS
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced in a throwaway container of sanarycriar/lms:local running only nginx. A rate-limited anonymous 40 MB POST to /api/v1/x showed a worker holding `/var/lib/nginx/tmp/client_body/0000000001 (deleted)` at 29,359,971 bytes mid-upload. That is before any upstream contact (502 only after the full body). The temp file is unlinked, so `du` and `ls` do not even show the usage. Caddy allows 6 GB on every cursos route, and nginx has client_max_body_size 6G with default proxy_request_buffering on. The temp path (--http-client-body-temp-path=/var/lib/nginx/tmp/client_body) is in the container's writable layer on the host disk. It is real, but the attacker must upload as many bytes as the free disk (tens of GB) and hold the connections open. The effect is transient: files are freed when the connections end, and Postgres and Redis recover once space returns. Downgraded to low.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/caddy/Caddyfile:99-101 `request_body { max_size 6GB }` site-wide; learnhouse/docker/nginx.conf:20 `client_max_body_size 6G`, :26 `client_body_buffer_size 32k`, no proxy_request_buffering off. Repro output: '7 /var/lib/nginx/tmp/client_body/0000000001 (deleted) 29359971 bytes'.
verdicts.fix: In the cursos block of the Caddyfile, set a small default and a large limit only on upload routes, for example: `@subidas path /api/v1/activities/* /api/v1/blocks/* /api/v1/courses/* /api/v1/orgs/* /api/v1/users/*` then `request_body @subidas { max_size 6GB }` and `request_body { max_size 25MB }`. Keep the global value small. In docker/nginx.conf (marked 'Sanar y Criar:'), lower the server-level client_max_body_size (for example 25m) and raise it to 6G only inside `location /api/v1`. Do not just turn buffering off: Starlette would then spool multipart bodies to /tmp, or read JSON into RAM, before auth.

verdicts.title: Off-site backups upload the .env secrets together with the full database, unencrypted and never pruned
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. backup.sh:68 copies the whole .env into the backup folder. :88 runs `rclone copy` of that folder to the remote with no encryption step, and retention (:79) only prunes local folders. crypto.py derives the Fernet key that encrypts the stored PayPal client secret as sha256(LEARNHOUSE_AUTH_JWT_SECRET_KEY). So a single off-site folder (env.respaldo + db.dump) gives JWT forging for admin sessions on the live site, the decrypted live PayPal secret, and all buyer data. The guide's only mitigation is 'usa un destino privado'. A Drive or B2 account compromise is a realistic threat for a small practice, and the copies pile up forever, including LEARNHOUSE_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD from before it is deleted.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/scripts/backup.sh:68 `cp -p "$SC_ENV_FILE" "$destino/env.respaldo"`, :79 local-only find/rm, :88 `rclone copy "$destino" "$remoto/$sello"`; apps/api/src/services/webhooks/crypto.py:19-23 `_fernet_key` = sha256(auth_jwt_secret_key); providers/paypal.py:133-138 decrypt_secret of client_secret_enc; docs/despliegue.md:202.
verdicts.fix: Upload only db.dump, content.tar.gz and SHA256SUMS: for example `rclone copy --exclude env.respaldo "$destino" "$remoto/$sello"`. The guide already says to keep .env in the password manager. Encrypt before upload: require SC_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT and run `age -r "$rcpt" -o db.dump.age db.dump` (same for content.tar.gz), or refuse remotes whose `rclone config show` type is not `crypt`. Add remote retention: `rclone delete --min-age "${dias}d" "$remoto" && rclone rmdirs "$remoto" --leave-root`.

verdicts.title: The documented daily backup cron line silently never runs until backups/ exists (first deploy never creates it)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: `sh -c 'cd DIR && ./scripts/backup.sh >> backups/backup.log 2>&1'` with no backups/ prints 'backups/backup.log: No such file or directory', exits 1, and the script never runs. The kit copied by the guide (despliegue.md:94-96: compose, caddy, scripts, .env.example, README) has no backups/ folder. The first deploy skips backup.sh because the DB is empty (actualizar.sh:72-73), and only backup.sh does `mkdir -p "$raiz"`. The guide's first-deploy step 7 sends the operator straight to installing the cron. So there are no automatic backups until the first later update or a manual run, and permanently none if SC_BACKUP_DIR is absolute. Cron mail usually goes nowhere, so the failure is silent. A plausible silent loss of backups for weeks of real sales.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/scripts/backup.sh:17 and docs/despliegue.md:200 cron line; backup.sh:35-36 is the only mkdir; actualizar.sh:72-73; repro: 'sh: line 1: backups/backup.log: No such file or directory' exit=1, ran.txt not created.
verdicts.fix: Change the documented cron line in backup.sh:17 and despliegue.md:200 to `15 3 * * * cd /opt/sanarycriar && mkdir -p backups && ./scripts/backup.sh >> backups/backup.log 2>&1`. Better: have backup.sh log by itself after `mkdir -p "$raiz"` with `exec >>"$raiz/backup.log" 2>&1`, and document `15 3 * * * /opt/sanarycriar/scripts/backup.sh`. Also create backups/ in the guide's scp/mkdir step, and optionally ping a healthcheck URL on success.

verdicts.title: Nothing in the production kit stops LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE=true (which re-enables the PayPal mock override and dev-only surfaces)
verdicts.reasoning: Partly mitigated: .env.example:42 ships `LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE=false` and :130-132 warns against the PAYPAL_* overrides. The /api/v1/dev endpoints are also superadmin-gated (routers/dev.py _require_superadmin). Still, nothing in compose or requerir_env enforces it, and config.py:234-242 reads it straight from the env. A single bad edit turns on the PayPal base override (settings.py:45-47, which would send live credentials elsewhere), /docs and openapi, the relaxed CSRF and the dev router. This is a cheap hardening against operator error, not an exploitable flaw by itself.
verdicts.evidence: deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml:28-37 (no LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE in environment:); deploy/scripts/_comun.sh:27-34 requerir_env; apps/api/src/services/payments/settings.py:45-47; deploy/.env.example:42.
verdicts.fix: Add `LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE: "false"` under learnhouse-app `environment:` in docker-compose.prod.yml (it overrides env_file). In requerir_env, add `if grep -Eiq '^LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE=["'\'']?(true|1|yes)' "$SC_ENV_FILE" || grep -Eq '^LEARNHOUSE_PAYPAL_(API|WEB)_BASE=' "$SC_ENV_FILE"; then fallar "..."; fi` (skipped when SC_COMPOSE_OVERRIDE is set, for local-smoke).

verdicts.title: Fernet key for the stored PayPal secret is derived from the JWT secret: rotating it breaks payments, and leaking it exposes PayPal
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. crypto.py:19-23 derives the Fernet key from sha256(auth_jwt_secret_key), and it is lru_cached. credentials_from_config raises SECRET_UNREADABLE when decryption fails (paypal.py:133-138), so after a JWT secret rotation checkout, capture and reconcile all fail until the secret is re-entered. .env.example:70 only says rotation closes sessions. The impact is operational and documentation-level, so low.
verdicts.evidence: apps/api/src/services/webhooks/crypto.py:19-23; providers/paypal.py:133-138; deploy/.env.example:70 '# Si cambias LEARNHOUSE_AUTH_JWT_SECRET_KEY se cierran todas las sesiones.'
verdicts.fix: Change .env.example:70 to also say: 'y hay que volver a pegar el Secret de PayPal en Pagos > Configuración; si este secreto se filtra, rota también el Secret en PayPal.' Add the same to the despliegue.md incident and rotation notes. Optionally add LEARNHOUSE_PAYMENTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY used by payments with MultiFernet([new, jwt-derived]) for existing rows.

verdicts.title: nginx access log inside the container stores password-reset codes, emails and magic-link tokens, with no rotation
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed in the built image: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:98 `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;` writes to a plain file (no symlink to stdout). docker/start.sh runs nginx in the background with no log redirect, so the compose json-file limits do not apply. The full request line, query string included, is logged. Exposure is limited: anyone who can read the container filesystem already has the .env, the file is reset on each container recreate (every update), and the codes are short-lived. The main effects are unbounded growth between updates and PII retention, so low.
verdicts.evidence: `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh sanarycriar/lms:local -c 'grep access_log /etc/nginx/nginx.conf; ls -la /var/log/nginx'` -> '98: access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;', /var/log/nginx is a normal dir; learnhouse/docker/start.sh:27 `nginx -g 'daemon off;' &`.
verdicts.fix: In learnhouse/docker/nginx.conf (marked 'Sanar y Criar:'), add at http level (outside server{}, since the file is included into http): `log_format sc_noargs '$remote_addr [$time_local] "$request_method $uri" $status $body_bytes_sent $request_time';` and inside server{}: `access_log /dev/stdout sc_noargs;`, or `access_log off;`.

verdicts.title: Supply chain: CI actions and runtime base images use mutable tags while the job holds packages:write
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. sanarycriar-image.yml pins actions/checkout, setup-buildx, login and build-push by version tags (lines 38, 65, 68, 75) with packages: write. Compose uses floating caddy:2-alpine and pgvector/pgvector:pg16, and actualizar.sh runs `dc pull` on every update. This is standard supply-chain hardening, not a present vulnerability. Floating pg16 minors also bring security fixes, so this is a trade-off. Low.
verdicts.evidence: .github/workflows/sanarycriar-image.yml:24-26, :38, :65, :68, :75; deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml:60, :109; deploy/scripts/actualizar.sh:104.
verdicts.fix: Pin each `uses:` to a full 40-char commit SHA with the version as a trailing comment (Renovate or Dependabot can bump them). In docker-compose.prod.yml, pin `caddy:2.x.y-alpine@sha256:<digest>` and `pgvector/pgvector:0.x.y-pg16@sha256:<digest>`, and update them deliberately.

verdicts.title: Platform container runs every service as root and the app connects to Postgres as a superuser
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. `id` in sanarycriar/lms:local gives uid=0, and there is no USER in the final runner stage (Dockerfile:75 onwards), so pm2, the API, ffmpeg, Next.js and collab run as root. Only the nginx workers drop to user nginx. POSTGRES_USER learnhouse is the bootstrap superuser of the official image, and the app uses it. This only increases the blast radius after a separate RCE or SQL injection, so it is defense-in-depth. Low.
verdicts.evidence: docker run ... sanarycriar/lms:local id -> uid=0(root); ps in container: master nginx root, workers nginx; deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml:35, :63.
verdicts.fix: In compose learnhouse-app add `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]`. Create a NOSUPERUSER app role through an init SQL mounted at /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d (new installs) or a one-off migration script (existing): `CREATE ROLE lh_app LOGIN PASSWORD ... NOSUPERUSER; ALTER DATABASE learnhouse OWNER TO lh_app; REASSIGN OWNED BY learnhouse TO lh_app;`, and point LEARNHOUSE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING at it. Note: CREATE EXTENSION vector needs a superuser, so create it once beforehand. Longer term, run the pm2 apps as a non-root user.

verdicts.title: Full PayPal 'payer' object (PayPal email, name, payer_id) stored on every order row and therefore in every backup
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. _MAX_RAW_KEYS includes 'payer' and 'purchase_units' (which carries payee and shipping). checkout.py:342 and fulfillment.py:350/414 store the trimmed payloads in sc_pay_order.raw. A grep shows 'payer' is never read anywhere else in api/src, so the data is unused and is purely a data-minimisation issue.
verdicts.evidence: apps/api/src/services/payments/providers/paypal.py:51, :89-93; services/payments/checkout.py:342; fulfillment.py:74-79, :350, :414; grep 'payer' in api/src only hits paypal.py:51 and :324 (links rel).
verdicts.fix: In paypal.py, remove "payer" from _MAX_RAW_KEYS. In _trim, also rebuild purchase_units keeping only reference_id, custom_id, amount and payments.captures[*].{id,status,amount,seller_receivable_breakdown,create_time}, dropping payee and shipping. Optionally add a one-off SQL to strip existing rows: `UPDATE sc_pay_order SET raw = raw #- '{capture,payer}' #- '{create,payer}' #- '{last_status,payer}'`.

checked_ok: PayPal mock is not reachable or usable in production: it is not in docker-compose.prod.yml, the dev/ files are not in the image, and settings.paypal_api_base()/paypal_web_base_override() only honor LEARNHOUSE_PAYPAL_API_BASE/WEB_BASE when development_mode is true. config.py parses LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE=false correctly, and config.yaml defaults to false. Rendered `docker compose config` shows LEARNHOUSE_DEVELOPMENT_MODE: "false".

Dev stack ports (Postgres 5433, Redis 6380, Mailpit, API 1338, mock 8099) are all bound to 127.0.0.1. dev/api.env and usuarios-prueba.local.env are gitignored by the parent .gitignore (dev/*.env), and `git ls-files` in the fork shows no tracked env, key or credential files.
Production compose publishes only 80/443(+udp) on Caddy. db, redis and learnhouse-app ports 9000/8000/4000 are internal only. The Caddy admin API listens on 127.0.0.1:2019 inside its own container.

`caddy validate` (caddy v2.11.7) reports Valid configuration. A live test with a throwaway Caddy plus curl on an isolated Docker network: //evil.com/, /%2F%2Fevil.com/, /%5C%5Cevil.com/, CRLF in path/query (/%0d%0aSet-Cookie...), /@evil.com on www and psicoinfantilve all redirect to absolute https://www.sanarycriarve.com/... (no open redirect, no header injection). Security headers are present on redirects and 404s.

Client IP for rate limiting: Caddy overwrites the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For (no trusted_proxies). The API takes the right-most non-private XFF hop and collab takes the left-most hop, and both resolve to the real client. X-Forwarded-Proto https comes through nginx's map, so cookies are Secure.

Credentialed CORS regex in single tenancy also admits http://localhost:*. Not exploitable because the auth cookies are SameSite=Lax, so a cross-site fetch from localhost carries no session. The marketing-site extra CORS is GET/HEAD only, without credentials.

Docker image hygiene: .dockerignore excludes **/.env*, logs and .git, the Dockerfile wipes apps/api/content, and the runtime-config.js written by server-wrapper.js only contains NEXT_PUBLIC_* plus LEARNHOUSE_PLATFORM_URL (no server secrets). The CI checkout token is not baked into the image because .git is excluded.

CI workflow: GITHUB_REF_NAME is used through an env var (no ${{ }} script injection). There is no pull_request or pull_request_target trigger with packages:write. Upstream workflows that need secrets (notify-infra, release, cli-publish) do not trigger on the sanarycriar branch or sc-v* tags.

shellcheck v0.10.0 -x -S style on _comun.sh, backup.sh, restaurar.sh, actualizar.sh, deploy-sitio.sh and smoke.sh: no findings. Tags and --version are regex-validated, SC_DIR_REMOTO is validated before ssh interpolation, and release-pruning rm -rf only targets date-named entries under releases/.
Backup permissions: umask 077, chmod 700 on the backup root, cp -p keeps .env at 600, fijar_env chmods its temp file to 600, and SHA256SUMS is verified on restore.

limpiar-datos-de-prueba.py refuses to run unless dev mode is on or --permitir-produccion is passed, defaults to a dry run, never deletes superadmin/Admin/Maintainer accounts, and uses parameterised SQL. configurar-organizacion.py refuses plain http for non-localhost, never prints the password, and reads env files without executing them.

local-smoke override (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, loopback ports) is never copied to the server (the scp list in despliegue.md excludes local-smoke), and it runs under its own compose project and volumes.

Static site: JSON-LD escapes '<' (seo.ts serializeJsonLd), catalog data goes through plainText() and safeHttpUrl() (only http/https thumbnails), offer hrefs are prefix-built with encodeURIComponent, and React islands use no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. CSP restricts connect/img to self + cursos. The quiz localStorage holds only A-D answers with a 7-day TTL, is validated on read, and is never sent anywhere. There are no forms that collect health data on the site.
Purchase confirmation email HTML-escapes the buyer name, offer and course names, URLs and the preheader. Payment logs reference order UUIDs, not buyer emails.
/content files are served by an access-controlled router (local_content.py) with nosniff, Content-Disposition and SVG CSP, not as a raw static mount.
